subject: Arcadia Health trial — traffic hypothesis, SLA mapping & success checklist
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Thompson <alyssa@arcadiahealth.org>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Arcadia trial — traffic hypothesis, SLA mapping & success checklist

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the demo call today. Very helpful to see the triage flows and high-level goals. As discussed I pulled together a short hypothesis + checklist so we can lock scope for the 6-week trial and avoid surprises on capacity/SLOs.

Quick recap / asks: 
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for Arcadia’s triage assistant with latency < 250ms p50 for short prompts and < 400ms p95 for standard patient-summary workloads while keeping $/k tokens target below the agreed cap.
- Primary success metrics (draft): 1) P95 latency under target on production-representative traffic; 2) semantic match > 90% on the 200-case eval set; 3) no functional regressions on hallucination tests.
- Data we need from you to map trial capacity: RPS (avg and peak), average prompt tokens, average response tokens, typical concurrency per operator session, and burst profile (e.g., 5 min peak every hour). Also please indicate percent of calls requiring long context (>4096 tokens) and percent of streaming vs. non-streaming responses.

Hypothesized traffic from our notes (please confirm):
- Avg steady RPS: 8-12 RPS
- Peak burst: up to 90 RPS for 2–5 min
- Avg tokens: prompt 220 tokens, response 320 tokens
- Concurrency: 12 active operator sessions, spikes to 60 during morning batch
- Long-context use: ~6% of calls

Proposed trial plan (timeline):
1) Week 0 (this week): exchange sample traffic snapshot + success criteria sheet (I attached both).
2) Week 1: Redwood to provision a trial cluster; we run warmup replay and sanity load.
3) Week 2–4: Controlled soak and verifications, plus 200-case eval run + qualitative review.
4) Week 5: Final SLA verification and cost report.
5) Week 6: Signoff + next-step commercial discussion.

Owners:
- Redwood AE: Priyom (me) — trial coordination and commercial questions
- Redwood CSM: Monica — onboarding, runbook, and report delivery
- Arcadia: Alyssa & Evan — provide traffic snapshot, eval set, and accept criteria

Can you confirm the real traffic numbers and whether the hypothesis above is in the right ballpark? If numbers differ significantly we’ll update the plan and capacity assumptions. Also flag any compliance or audit evidence you’ll need while this runs in our hosted trial.

Attachments: poc_success_criteria.xlsx, sample_traffic_snapshot.json, redwood_trial_scope.pdf

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priym@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199
From: Alyssa Thompson <alyssa@arcadiahealth.org>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@arcadiahealth.org>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Arcadia trial — traffic hypothesis, SLA mapping & success checklist

Thanks Priyom — this is very clear and the plan looks reasonable. Quick data points from our side (see attached sample_traffic_snapshot.json which is a 24h rolling export):
- Avg steady RPS: 10 RPS (measured across 24h)
- Typical peak bursts: 85–100 RPS for 3–6 minutes, mostly between 07:00-09:00 ET and 18:00-20:00 ET
- Avg tokens: prompt 180 tokens, response 300 tokens
- Concurrency: usually 14 active operator sessions, peaks to 72 during morning batch processing
- Long-context: ~9% of calls reference >4096 token context (histor medical notes attached inline)
- Streaming: ~40% streaming (progressive patient summary), rest non-streaming

A few clarifications / asks:
1) For the long-context calls, can Redwood suggest a fallback model/flow that keeps latency under control?
2) We need the trial to demonstrate audit logs for token-level tracing and a 30-day retention policy for logs — please confirm.
3) Who will own the evaluation rubric on our side? I propose Evan lead the eval and I’ll coordinate logistics.

We attached the traffic JSON and a short eval seed set (200 anonymized records) to the pilot inbox. Let us know if you need different formats.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Thompson
Director, Clinical Automation | Arcadia Health
alyssa@arcadiahealth.org
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Thompson <alyssa@arcadiahealth.org>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@arcadiahealth.org>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Arcadia trial — traffic hypothesis, SLA mapping & success checklist

Great — thanks for the snapshot, Alyssa. That aligns closely with our hypothesis; we’ll tweak a few capacity knobs for the higher morning peaks. Quick answers and next steps below: 

1) Long-context strategy: we recommend a two-path flow — preferred: quantized context model (8-bit) on larger memory nodes for true long-context calls; fallback: 1) summarize older notes into a condensed prompt (we can deliver a summarization microservice), or 2) route to a smaller, faster model with explicit context window and an appended summary. I added the proposed model mapping to redwood_trial_scope.pdf.

2) Audit/logs: we can provide token-level tracing and a 30-day retention policy in the trial. We’ll surface an exportable CSV and S3 snapshot for each trial run. Monica will share the audit runbook.

3) Evaluation ownership: acknowledged — Evan as Arcadia evaluator; we’ll coordinate with Evan to schedule the 200-case eval during Week 3.

Proposed milestone dates (adjustable):
- Wed 2027-05-05: Redwood cluster provisioned + warmup replay
- Mon 2027-05-10: Controlled soak begins
- Mon 2027-05-17: 200-case eval run (Evan leads)
- Tue 2027-05-25: Final verification report delivered

Monica / Ben — can one of you own provisioning and the trial runbook? I’ll set the HubSpot milestone and calendar invites once we lock dates. Alyssa/Evan — please confirm if the dates above work and whether you need us to pick a specific 4-hour window for the morning peak test.

Thanks,
Priyom
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Thompson <alyssa@arcadiahealth.org>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@arcadiahealth.org>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Arcadia trial — traffic hypothesis, SLA mapping & success checklist

Forwarding the confirmed plan and adding the operational checklist. We will: 
- Provision trial cluster on 5/5 (Ben will own infra provisioning).
- Run warmup and schedule a replay of the attached sample_traffic_snapshot.json to validate burst behavior.
- Provide an audit runbook and token-level export (S3 link) by 5/6.
- Run the 200-case eval on 5/17; please provide the evaluation rubric by 5/12 so we can instrument the run.

Operational notes: 
- Ben: please size GPUs for 100 RPS peak with headroom and include quantized nodes for long-context handling.
- Priyom: I’ll create the trial runbook and a Slack channel (redwood-arcadia-poc).
- Arcadia: please confirm whether the morning peak test should be run at 08:00 ET or 09:00 ET (we prefer 08:00 ET to catch your busiest window).

Next steps / actions: 
- Alyssa: confirm 4 traffic items above + share any compliance templates we should prefill.
- Evan: confirm evaluation rubric owner and share any preferred scoring metrics (precision/recall/Kendall/semantic match).
- Ben: start infra sizing and share expected costs for the 6-week trial by EOD 5/3.

Thanks everyone — I’ll post the Slack invite and calendar events once dates are locked.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai
